plate_comment: Wastegate solenoid duty controller, called once per phase group A through cm848_turboCompensationWrapper: writes rpm_governor_state_t_0040a3ca.commanded_rpm, the wastegate duty request in half-duty counts (12800 = 100 %; cm848_applyWastegateSolenoidDuty sends 2 x it). commanded_rpm = clamp(calibration base + rate-limited term + PI integrator fed by the fuel_demand_quantity and fuel_flow_rate error terms, lower_rpm_limit, desired_rpm); the ceiling is wastegate_duty_ceiling_fixed x a battery-voltage gain (or the engine speed x load grid when wastegate_duty_ceiling_grid_enable_cal is set), the floor is wastegate_duty_floor_fixed or its grid, and both are trimmed by altitude (barometric_altitude_feet). (was cm848_boostCompensatedRpmGovernor)
evidence: rpm_governor_state_t.commanded_rpm (0x40a3ca) is written only by this function (xref: this function and the init function) and read by cm848_applyWastegateSolenoidDuty as duty = 2 x it (25600 = 100 %, output channel 11, P0243 read-back). The RAM dump closes the loop numerically: battery 192 (12.0 V) gives gain 4649 (interpolated between 5202 at 10 V and 4096 at 14 V), 9600 x 4649 / 4096 = 10896, and wastegate_solenoid_duty_command (0x40c14e) = 21792 = 2 x 10896 exactly. A ceiling scaled by battery voltage and by altitude only makes sense for a solenoid duty, not an rpm. A second reader, cm848_calculateSpeedControlLimit, clamps the same word in the same half-duty units (see note); it does not change this verdict.

plate_comment: Wastegate (CWG) boost-pressure monitor, called from periodicTaskSet_fuelDemand; it runs only when cold_start_feature_flags mask 0x8, protection_feature_status_flags mask 0x1000000 and the start battery temperature test (DAT_003fd270) allow it, and it clears its counts and exits while sensor faults or the wastegate solenoid fault (403) are active. It looks up three boost limits by barometric_pressure_reference and sets fault 332 (fault_detected_bits_320_to_335 mask 0x1000, high boost) after wastegate_monitor_debounce_count_limit passes with boost at or above wastegate_monitor_fail_high_boost_pressure_threshold, engine speed at or above wastegate_monitor_minimum_engine_speed_threshold and wastegate_solenoid_duty_command at or below DAT_00409fe0. It also counts the passes (wastegate_monitor_pass_event_count, wastegate_monitor_pass_duration_count) in which boost stays between the pass-low and pass-high thresholds at engine load of at least DAT_00409fe4; boost is intake_manifold_pressure, or boost_pressure_above_barometric when protection_sensor_mode_flag is set. (was hpcr_fuelDemandProc)
evidence: Every role in the code has a counterpart in the e2m CWG (Controlled WasteGate) monitor parameter list; the pairing is by role (the e2m uses different addresses), not by address: CWG_Monitor_Enable (cold_start_feature_flags mask 0x8), CWG_Min_Start_Battery_Temp_Threshold (DAT_00409fe8 = 1280 = 20 F against battery_temperature_sensor_filtered, latched in cm848_initAdaptiveControl), CWG_Driver_Duty_Cycle_Threshold (DAT_00409fe0 = 11520 = 45 % against the duty command), CWG_Minimum_Engine_Speed_Threshold (14400 = 1800 rpm), CWG_High_Load_Threshold (DAT_00409fe4 = 19200 = 75 %), the Fail / Pass-high / Pass-low boost tables by ambient pressure, CWG_High_Boost_Error (mask 0x1000 in fault bits 320..335) and CWG_Total_Pass_Counter / CWG_Total_Pass_Time. The guard on fault_detected_bits_400_to_415 & 8 is fault 403, the wastegate solenoid read-back fault (P0243). Its sibling cm848_monitorOverboostAndHighLoadBoostBand is the non-CWG (P0234) variant. In the dump (engine off, runtime RAM) protection_feature_status_flags mask 0x1000000 is clear, so the monitor was not armed at that moment and all its counters read 0.

plate_comment: Per-state duty calculation of the 4-state charging-voltage (alternator field) regulator whose state machine is cm848_dispatchProtectionOutputMode; it runs only while engine_feature_enable_flags_cal bit 0 is set and writes alternator_field_duty_target (25600 = 100 %), clamped to 25600: state 0 (engine stopped, or fault 368) gives 0, or protection_fuel_output_idle_cal while fault 368 is set; state 1 gives the soft-start ramp by pass count; state 2 gives the duty from charging_voltage_error through alternator_field_duty_regulation_*; state 3 gives the load-response duty for an rpm-dependent hold time, then the slow-average snapshot plus an rpm- and duty-scaled ramp. It also keeps alternator_field_duty_slow_average. When operating_mode_flags mask 0x20 is set (it is in the dump), cm848_calculateProtectionOutputDemand's PID loop replaces the duty in states 2 and 3. (was cm848_filterProtectionOutput)
evidence: Called in phase group B between cm848_dispatchProtectionOutputMode (state machine, handlers at ROM 0x38338 / 0x38384 / 0x383f0 / 0x3844c, disassembled) and cm848_applyAlternatorFieldDuty (output channel 27, field control pin); every table it reads is an alternator_field_* table, indexed by battery_voltage_delta = battery_voltage_prev (charging voltage target) - battery_voltage, or by engine speed. It does not filter the output; the only filtering is a 0.1-weight EMA (coefficient 6554 / 65536) of the duty kept for the load response. Dump: target 240 (15.0 V) minus battery 192 (12.0 V) = delta 48; engine_feature_enable_flags_cal = 0x27EF has bit 0 set.

plate_comment: Intake (grid) air heater performance test, a 7-state machine in intake_air_heater_performance_test_state (0 armed, 1 baseline taken, 2 heater on, 3 heater off, 4 passed, 5 failed, 6 aborted) that samples battery-voltage ADC channel index 4 in threes while the heater relays switch on and off; it runs only when operating_mode_flags mask 0x200 is set (clear in the dump) and hpcr_throttlePositionDiagnostic armed it at start. If the voltage drop at turn-on and the recovery after turn-off agree within DAT_00064430 counts, then both below the intake_air_heater_performance_threshold_* value for the intake manifold temperature sets fault 411 (fault_detected_bits_400_to_415 mask 0x800, P2609; state 5) and anything else clears it (state 4); if the two disagree the test ends in state 6 and leaves the fault bit unchanged. engine_protection_batteryLoad_check also aborts the test (state 6) when voltage, temperature or heater state is out of range, and a steady result in state 4 or 5 sets diagnostic_monitor_complete_bits 0x400. (was hpcr_injectPressureTuning)
evidence: State 0 samples qadc_channel_index_table[4] (slot 4 = battery voltage, the channel of battery_voltage_linearization_*) before the heater relays are energised (cm848_countDownIntakeAirHeaterPreheat holds logical outputs 43/44 off while operating_mode_flags & 0x200 and the state is 0), states 1 and 2 sample it with the heater on, state 3 after intake_air_heater_preheat_remaining_ticks reaches 0; the final compare against hpcr_pressure_diag_lookup_ref (table intake_air_heater_performance_threshold_axis / _values by intake_manifold_temperature_sensor_filtered: 45 counts at 0 F falling to 24 at 66 F) sets or clears fault_detected_bits_400_to_415 & 0x800 = fault 411. Nothing in the function touches a pressure, so the hpcr_pressure_diag_* names are wrong-domain. Fault 411 = P2609 is taken from the lead and the campaign file; I did not decode the DTC slot table myself.

Written only by cm848_dispatchProtectionOutputMode (next state from the 4-entry handler table at ROM 0x57730) and cm848_initProtectionFilterValues; all six readers are the charging regulator cluster (dispatch, filter, PID, output checks, processProtectionMode2). Values 0..3: 0 idle / fault, 1 start ramp, 2 regulation, 3 load response. Dump: 0 (engine off).
Written only by cm848_dispatchProtectionOutputMode (copy of the state before the handler runs); read by the filter (state 3 entry test) and the PID (state 1 -> 2 integrator preset).

Loaded on the first pass of state 3 from alternator_field_load_response_hold_time_* indexed by engine speed, decremented once per pass while non-zero; while non-zero the duty follows alternator_field_duty_load_response_*, at 0 the load response moves to its ramp stage. Used only in cm848_filterProtectionOutput and the init function.

0 outside state 3, set to 1 on state 3 entry (hold stage, duty from the load-response table), set to 2 when the hold timer expires (duty restored to the slow-average snapshot, then ramped); zeroed in states 0 and 2. Not a fault state; only cm848_filterProtectionOutput and the init function touch it.

Only user is cm848_filterProtectionOutput: it is the x input of the alternator_field_duty_start_ramp_* lookup in state 1, incremented once per pass there and zeroed in states 0 and 2, so it is the age of the soft-start ramp (not a voltage scan).

ema = (ema x (65536 - coefficient) + alternator_field_duty_target x coefficient) / 65536 at the top of cm848_filterProtectionOutput, coefficient = cold_start_fuel_ema_coeff_cal = 6554 (0.1); nothing to do with cold start or fuel. Read only to take the snapshot below.

Copy of the slow average duty taken on entry to regulator state 3; written back into alternator_field_duty_target when the load-response hold timer expires (stage 1 -> 2). Only user is cm848_filterProtectionOutput.

Incremented once per pass in regulator state 3 and zeroed in states 0, 1 and 2; read by the state 3 handler (ROM 0x3844c): with the duty at 25600 and this count above the limit at 0x4087b0 the machine leaves state 3 for state 2. It counts time in the load response, not a confirmation of anything.

Written only in cm848_processProtectionCoolantLookup: charging_voltage_target_by_battery_temperature_* lookup on battery_temperature_sensor_filtered plus charging_voltage_target_offset (or battery_voltage_correction_default_cal when battery_voltage_correction_enable_cal is non-zero). Read in cm848_processProtectionVoltageOffset as delta = battery_voltage_prev - battery voltage and in the SCI command 20 reply. Dump check: battery temperature 2086 (32.6 F) interpolates 236 -> 232 to 235.65, + offset 4 = 240 = 15.0 V, which is the stored value.

cm848_processProtectionVoltageOffset: battery_voltage_delta = battery_voltage_prev (target) - sensor_readings_t.battery_voltage, signed, 1/16 V per count; the input of the state 2 and state 3 duty tables and of the PID. Dump: 240 - 192 = 48.

cm848_processProtectionVoltageOffset: EMA of battery_voltage_delta with battery_voltage_filter_coeff_cal; it is a filtered charging voltage ERROR, not a filtered battery voltage (the checks compare it with thresholds the way an error is compared).

cm848_processProtectionVoltageOffset: battery_voltage_delta - battery_voltage_filtered (the error minus its slow average); the state 2 handler (ROM 0x383f0) enters state 3 when it exceeds the threshold at 0x4087ac, i.e. a fast voltage dip from an electrical load.

First argument of lookupTableInterpolation (ROM 0x55ef4 reads it as the starting segment, writes back 2 x index: lhz r12,0(r8) ... sth r12,0(r8)); initialised to 2 in cm848_initProtectionFilterValues; its only other reference is the charging_voltage_target_by_battery_temperature_* lookup in cm848_processProtectionCoolantLookup. Nothing to do with CAN. (Existing 'Lookup cache' comment wording in global_variables.csv says 'the last axis segment offset (2 x index)'.)

First argument of lookupTableInterpolation (ROM 0x55ef4 reads it as the starting segment, writes back 2 x index: lhz r12,0(r8) ... sth r12,0(r8)); initialised to 2 in cm848_initProtectionFilterValues; its only other reference is the alternator_field_duty_start_ramp_* lookup (state 1). Nothing to do with CAN. (Existing 'Lookup cache' comment wording in global_variables.csv says 'the last axis segment offset (2 x index)'.)

First argument of lookupTableInterpolation (ROM 0x55ef4 reads it as the starting segment, writes back 2 x index: lhz r12,0(r8) ... sth r12,0(r8)); initialised to 2 in cm848_initProtectionFilterValues; its only other reference is the alternator_field_duty_regulation_* lookup (state 2). Nothing to do with CAN. (Existing 'Lookup cache' comment wording in global_variables.csv says 'the last axis segment offset (2 x index)'.)

First argument of lookupTableInterpolation (ROM 0x55ef4 reads it as the starting segment, writes back 2 x index: lhz r12,0(r8) ... sth r12,0(r8)); initialised to 2 in cm848_initProtectionFilterValues; its only other reference is the alternator_field_load_response_hold_time_* lookup (state 3 entry). Nothing to do with CAN. (Existing 'Lookup cache' comment wording in global_variables.csv says 'the last axis segment offset (2 x index)'.)

First argument of lookupTableInterpolation (ROM 0x55ef4 reads it as the starting segment, writes back 2 x index: lhz r12,0(r8) ... sth r12,0(r8)); initialised to 2 in cm848_initProtectionFilterValues; its only other reference is the alternator_field_duty_load_response_* lookup (state 3 hold). Nothing to do with CAN. (Existing 'Lookup cache' comment wording in global_variables.csv says 'the last axis segment offset (2 x index)'.)

First argument of lookupTableInterpolation (ROM 0x55ef4 reads it as the starting segment, writes back 2 x index: lhz r12,0(r8) ... sth r12,0(r8)); initialised to 2 in cm848_initProtectionFilterValues; its only other reference is the alternator_field_load_response_ramp_by_rpm_* lookup (state 3 ramp). Nothing to do with CAN. (Existing 'Lookup cache' comment wording in global_variables.csv says 'the last axis segment offset (2 x index)'.)

First argument of lookupTableInterpolation (ROM 0x55ef4 reads it as the starting segment, writes back 2 x index: lhz r12,0(r8) ... sth r12,0(r8)); initialised to 2 in cm848_initProtectionFilterValues; its only other reference is the alternator_field_load_response_ramp_by_duty_* lookup (state 3 ramp). Nothing to do with CAN. (Existing 'Lookup cache' comment wording in global_variables.csv says 'the last axis segment offset (2 x index)'.)
Weight of the new duty sample in the slow average (6554 / 65536 = 0.1 in the dump). Address 0x4087d2 is outside the EEPROM mirror 0x3fd482-0x3feec1, so the _cal suffix is dropped.

Behaviour is certain, the right name is not: it is read only in regulator state 0, where alternator_field_duty_target = this value, then forced to 0 unless fault_detected_bits_368_to_383 mask 0x1 is set (the state handlers return to state 0 whenever that fault is set). Value 0 in the dump. What fault 368 means is only inferred from cm848_processProtectionMode2, so I give no new name; 'idle' is at least not wrong for state 0. Address 0x4087fa is outside the EEPROM mirror, so any new name must not end in _cal.
Output of the wastegate_monitor_fail_high_boost_pressure_* lookup by barometric reference; boost at or above it (with the other conditions) counts toward fault 332 (CWG_High_Boost_Error).

Output of the wastegate_monitor_pass_high_boost_pressure_* lookup; upper edge of the PASS window (boost above it decrements the pass debounce), not a fault limit. e2m CWG_Pass_High_Boost_Pressure_Threshold.
Output of the wastegate_monitor_pass_low_boost_pressure_* lookup; lower edge of the PASS window. e2m CWG_Pass_Low_Boost_Pressure_Threshold.

Up/down counter of the high-boost check (+1 per qualifying pass up to the limit, -1 otherwise); at the limit it sets fault 332, at 0 it clears it. Address 0x3fd26c is RAM below the EEPROM mirror, so no _cal.
Up/down counter of the pass-window check (boost inside the window at load >= DAT_00409fe4 and rpm >= minimum); reaching the limit counts one pass event. It is the pass debounce, not a fault debounce.
Incremented each time wastegate_monitor_pass_debounce_count newly reaches the limit; written only by this function and its init. Matches e2m CWG_Total_Pass_Counter.
Incremented every pass while the pass debounce is at or above the limit (saturates at 0xffff), so it is the time spent inside the pass window; its role matches e2m CWG_Total_Pass_Time.
Engine speed (0.125 rpm per count; 14400 = 1800 rpm) below which both checks stop counting up; e2m CWG_Minimum_Engine_Speed_Threshold. Read only by this function.
30 passes in the dump; the limit for both the high-boost debounce and the pass debounce. Read only by this function.

Not a fuel pressure. Dump numbers: 0x40a196 = 1647 and its source boost_pressure_fuel_working (0x40a162) = 1648, against sensor_readings_t.barometric_pressure (0x40baf6) = 1647 and intake_manifold_pressure (0x40baf2) = 1700, with the offset boost_fuel_pressure_offset_lookup = 0. Code: it is clamped to 0x75e = 1886 counts = 101.6 kPa (standard sea-level atmosphere at 1/18.56 kPa per count), and the table 0x3ff080 -> 0x3ff0a2 that hpcr_fuelFinal_exponentialAverage applies to it reproduces the standard-atmosphere altitude in feet exactly (see governor_adjustment_input). It also indexes the three wastegate monitor tables. Used by about 14 functions, so rename it everywhere.

Written only by hpcr_injectPressureTuning (states 1..5), engine_protection_batteryLoad_check (abort = 6) and hpcr_throttlePositionDiagnostic (arms it: 0, or 6 when the battery and intake manifold temperatures disagree); cm848_computeIntakeAirHeaterPreheatDuration and cm848_countDownIntakeAirHeaterPreheat only read it (state 0 with operating_mode_flags & 0x200 holds relays 43/44 off for the baseline sample; 4, 5 and 6 release them). The existing CSV comment attributing the state machine to cm848_computeIntakeAirHeaterPreheatDuration and to 'intake-air-temp protection' is wrong.

Dwell countdown between test phases, reloaded from ROM DAT_0006442a / 00064424 / 00064428 (25 / 30 / 2); used by hpcr_injectPressureTuning and initialised from DAT_0006442c in hpcr_throttlePositionDiagnostic.
Counts the three battery-voltage ADC samples that are averaged in each phase.
Index (wraps after 3) of the three-element sample ring at 0x3fd1f6 filled in state 2.
State 0 accumulates three raw battery-voltage ADC samples (qadc channel index 4) taken before the heater relays are on, then divides by 3 in place; state 1 subtracts the loaded average from it.

Average battery-voltage ADC reading with the heater on (state 1, refreshed from the ring average at the end of state 2); state 2 checks the ring average against it (-DAT_0006442e / +DAT_00064438) and state 3 subtracts it from the after-turn-off average. It is a voltage, not a pressure.
State 3 accumulates three battery-voltage ADC samples after the heater relays are off, divides by 3 in place, and the recovery (this minus the loaded average) goes to DAT_0040b9e6.
hpcr_pressure_diag_sample_sum_state0 minus the loaded average (baseline minus loaded), taken in state 1; compared with the turn-off recovery and with the temperature threshold in state 3.

Output of the intake_air_heater_performance_threshold_* lookup by intake_manifold_temperature_sensor_filtered (45 counts at 0 F ... 24 at 66 F), taken once on the state 0 -> 1 move; the test fails when both the turn-on drop and the turn-off recovery are below it.

Element 4 of a per-slot forced-reading array that starts at 0x40bc80 (2 bytes per slot): it replaces the QADC index 4 (battery voltage) reading when diagnostic_service_dispatch_table word +72 mask 0x10 is set, in the heater test and in cm848_sciCommand20Callback case 10. The same pattern for slot 69 in SCI case 1 reads DAT_0040bd0a with word +80 mask 0x20, and 0x40bd0a - 0x40bc88 = 130 = 2 x (69 - 4), while the enable bits are slot / 16 words past +72 and bit slot mod 16 (slot 4 = +72 mask 0x10, slot 69 = +80 mask 0x20), so this is the battery-voltage slot's forced value. It is a raw ADC count (it stands in for the dispatch-table ADC reading).

Read only in cm848_boostCompensatedRpmGovernor: 0 selects the battery-voltage-scaled fixed ceiling (battery_voltage_correction_cal x gain / 4096), non-zero selects the engine speed x load grid (rpm_governor_state.reserved_0c). 0 in the dump. Address is in the EEPROM mirror, so _cal is right.

Read only in cm848_boostCompensatedRpmGovernor: non-zero takes the floor from the wastegate_duty_floor_* grid (rpm_governor_state.reserved_0e), 0 uses the fixed throttle_fuel_demand_alt_cal. 0 in the dump. EEPROM mirror.

Read only in cm848_boostCompensatedRpmGovernor (with fuel_mode_switch_state = 0): 0 leaves the ceiling and floor as computed, non-zero adds adjustment_delta to the ceiling and limit_adjustment to the floor (both lookups of governor_adjustment_input = altitude) and clamps to 0..12800. 0 in the dump. EEPROM mirror.

Read only in cm848_boostCompensatedRpmGovernor: the fixed floor of the wastegate duty request used when the floor grid is off; 128 half-duty counts = 1 % duty in the dump. Address is above the EEPROM mirror, so no _cal.
Read only in cm848_boostCompensatedRpmGovernor: the fixed ceiling (9600 = 75 % duty) multiplied by the battery voltage gain / 4096 when the ceiling grid is off. Above the EEPROM mirror, so no _cal.

x axis (battery voltage EMA, 1/16 V: 0 / 160 / 224 / 240 / 256) of the gain lookup in cm848_boostCompensatedRpmGovernor; its only reader. Address 0x4002ca is outside the EEPROM mirror, so the _cal suffix is wrong.

Q12 gain values (5202 / 5202 / 4096 / 4096 / 4096 = 1.27 at or below 10 V, 1.0 at or above 14 V) multiplied into the fixed duty ceiling; only reader is cm848_boostCompensatedRpmGovernor. Not EEPROM, so no _cal.

x axis of the lookup whose x input is governor_adjustment_input (altitude in feet), not engine speed; result rpm_governor_state.limit_adjustment is added to the duty floor. Only reader is cm848_boostCompensatedRpmGovernor. Mirrors wastegate_duty_ceiling_adjustment_by_altitude_axis. Not EEPROM, so no _cal.
Values of the same lookup (see governor_adjustment_rpm_axis_cal); only reader is cm848_boostCompensatedRpmGovernor. Not EEPROM, so no _cal.

Written by hpcr_fuelFinal_exponentialAverage from fuel_pressure_sensor_reference through the 0x3ff080 -> 0x3ff0a2 table, which I checked: 1105 / 1149 / 1196 / 1244 / 1293 / 1344 / 1396 / 1452 / 1507 counts (1/18.56 kPa) give 14000 / 13000 / 12000 / 11000 / 10000 / 9000 / 8000 / 7000 / 6000, and the standard atmosphere gives 13995 / 13014 / 12000 / 10998 / 10006 / 9005 / 8016 / 6984 / 6001 ft for those pressures. Read by the wastegate controller (both altitude trims) and by governor_adjustment_compare / _blend_check / fuel_demandBlend_weight_calc.

text: struct rpm_governor_state_t (0x40a3ca) is the wastegate duty controller state, all in half-duty counts (12800 = 100 %, the output stage sends 2 x commanded_rpm = 25600): commanded_rpm = final request; desired_rpm = duty ceiling; lower_rpm_limit = duty floor; reserved_0c = ceiling grid lookup (wastegate_duty_ceiling_*: x engine speed, y engine_load_input_b); reserved_0e = floor grid lookup; adjustment_delta = ceiling trim by altitude; limit_adjustment = floor trim by altitude; base_rpm_lookup = ceiling by engine speed alone (governor_base_rpm_output_cal, used while fuel_mode_switch_state is non-zero, floor then = throttle_rate_pid_gain_cal word 2); reserved_02 = feedback limit (smaller of throttle_rate_filtered_sum, reserved_04 and governor_rpm_state_output); reserved_04 = P minus D term of fuel_pressure_demand_reference - fuel_demand_quantity, +-25600; reserved_06 = P gain lookup. The struct and its 'rpm' fields should be renamed (e.g. wastegate_duty_state_t with duty-based field names); not proposed here.

Dump numbers for the wastegate path: fuel_feature_control_flags = 0x11DC (mask 0x1000 set, output stage enabled); wastegate_duty_ceiling_grid and _floor_grid are flat 11532 (90.1 % duty) with a last row of 0 and both grid enable flags are 0, so the grids are unused; ceiling = 9600 x battery gain, floor = 128. cm848_applyWastegateSolenoidDuty output = 21792 (85.1 %) at 12.0 V, exactly 2 x (9600 x 4649 / 4096).

Second reader of the wastegate duty request: rpm_governor_state_t.commanded_rpm is also read by cm848_calculateSpeedControlLimit (0x2ca14). It clamps the word with speed_control_rpm_upper_limit_cal (12800 = 100 % in half-duty counts) and, when governor_status_flags mask 0x4000 is set, into the window [fuel_control_setpoint_cal, 0x3200 - fuel_control_setpoint_cal] = [1856, 10944] (about 14.5 - 85.5 % duty), i.e. in the same half-duty units; the result fuel_control_setpoint_working (0x40b020) feeds cm848_calculateSpeedControlRampUp / RampDown, cm848_selectSpeedControlGains and cm848_checkSpeedZeroCondition (the governor_* speed / fuel PID ending in governor_fuel_demand_raw -> cm848_selectFuelControlModeOutput). Its purpose is unknown; it is a second consumer in duty units, not a contradiction of the wastegate reading, and the wastegate verdict does not depend on it (the only writer of 0x40a3ca is this function, the only actuator reader is the wastegate output stage). Do not rename the SpeedControl chain on this evidence; it needs its own review.

cm848_checkSpeedBandCondition (0x11a4c) is the integrator anti-windup of this controller: it sets throttle_acceleration_active_flag (integrator enabled) unless commanded_rpm is pinned at desired_rpm / lower_rpm_limit in the direction of the error. cm848_turboCompensationWrapper (0x1231c, phase group A) and mpc555_initTurboCompensationVariables (0x1233c) are its wrapper and init and should follow the rename (e.g. cm848_runWastegateDutyControl / cm848_initWastegateDutyControl). The throttle_rate_* and governor_rpm_band_* variables inside it are controller internals with misleading names; I did not rename them (no independent evidence for what their inputs measure).

Charging regulator chain, evidence from disassembly of the four state handlers (ROM 0x38338 / 0x38384 / 0x383f0 / 0x3844c) and the dump: next state 0 -> 1 when engine speed >= the threshold at 0x4087a8 or cold_start_phase = 3, and fault 368 clear; every state falls back to 0 when speed < the threshold at 0x4087a2 or fault 368 is set; 1 -> 2 when the duty reaches 25600 or battery_voltage_delta <= the threshold at 0x4087ae; 2 -> 3 when battery_voltage_delta_filtered > the threshold at 0x4087ac; 3 -> 2 when the duty is 25600 and the elapsed count exceeds the limit at 0x4087b0, or battery_voltage_delta <= 0x4087ae. The regulator is enabled by engine_feature_enable_flags_cal bit 0 (0x27EF in the dump; its CSV comment lists bits 2 / 6 / 13 only), and operating_mode_flags mask 0x20 (set in the dump) switches states 2 and 3 to the PID in cm848_calculateProtectionOutputDemand. cm848_processProtectionCoolantLookup (0x375c8) is the charging voltage target (battery temperature table + offset), cm848_processProtectionVoltageOffset (0x37658) the error, cm848_dispatchProtectionOutputMode (0x376dc) the state machine and cm848_calculateProtectionOutputDemand (0x37a40) the PID; suggested names: cm848_calculateChargingVoltageTarget, cm848_calculateChargingVoltageError, cm848_updateAlternatorFieldRegulatorState, cm848_calculateAlternatorFieldDutyPid.

Existing CSV comment to fix: alternator_field_duty_target (0x40b266) says it is 'filtered by cm848_filterProtectionOutput'; that function calculates the per-state duty and does not filter it. operating_mode_flags (0x3fd5ee) is inside the EEPROM mirror (EEPROM 0x16c) and has no _cal suffix; its bits seen here: 0x20 = charging PID enable, 0x200 = heater performance test enable, 0x400 = overboost monitor enable (value 0x7CA6 in the dump: 0x20 set, 0x200 clear). cold_start_feature_flags (0x3fd5c2) mask 0x8 = wastegate monitor enable (0x8488 in the dump, set); protection_feature_status_flags (0x40b9d0, runtime RAM) mask 0x1000000 = wastegate monitor armed, mask 0x4 = overboost monitor armed; both were clear in the dump (engine off), so nothing can be said about them while running.

Unnamed ROM / RAM words in the wastegate monitor (no global_variables.csv row, so no rename proposed): DAT_00409fe0 = wastegate driver duty threshold (11520 = 45 %, e2m CWG_Driver_Duty_Cycle_Threshold), DAT_00409fe4 = high load threshold (19200 = 75 %, 1/256 % units), DAT_00409fe8 = minimum start battery temperature (1280 = 20 F, 1/64 F), DAT_003fd270 = monitor armed flag (byte, set in cm848_initAdaptiveControl), DAT_003fd271 / 003fd273 / 003fd275 = lookup index caches of the three monitor tables. In the heater test: DAT_00064424 = 30, DAT_00064426 = 1 (preheat ticks left at which state 2 moves to 3), DAT_00064428 = 2, DAT_0006442a = 25, DAT_0006442e = 15 (lower tolerance of the loaded average), DAT_00064430 = 10 (max turn-on drop vs turn-off recovery difference), DAT_00064432 = 0 (minimum intake manifold temperature), DAT_00064434 = 208 (13.0 V max) and DAT_00064436 = 160 (10.0 V min) battery voltage for a valid test, DAT_00064438 = 10 (upper tolerance), DAT_0040b9e6 = turn-off recovery, DAT_003fd1ee = latest state 2 ring average, DAT_003fd1f6 = the 3-word sample ring.

hpcr_throttlePositionDiagnostic (0x53227c) is the arming step of the heater performance test, not a throttle diagnostic: it zeroes the sample count, ring index, hpcr_pressure_diag_reference_avg and hpcr_pressure_diag_sample_sum_state0, loads the dwell from DAT_0006442c, and sets the state to 0 only when the battery temperature and the intake manifold temperature agree within DAT_0006443a (a cold-soaked engine) and fault_detected_bits_368_to_383 bits 0x800 / 0x1000 are clear, otherwise to 6. Suggested name: cm848_armIntakeAirHeaterPerformanceTest (values of DAT_0006442c / DAT_0006443a not read).

engine_protection_batteryLoad_check (0x53232c) is not a battery load check: it returns 1 and sets the heater test state to 6 (aborted) when intake manifold temperature is below DAT_00064432, any of fault bits 16..31 & 0x18 / 288..303 & 0x3c0 is set, battery voltage is outside 10-13 V (DAT_00064436 / DAT_00064434), or the heater is neither in preheat-on nor preheat-done. Suggested name: cm848_checkIntakeAirHeaterPerformanceTestConditions (not verified beyond the code). Also boost_pressure_fuel_working (0x40a162) reads 1648 in the dump against barometric_pressure 1647 and intake_manifold_pressure 1700, so it holds the barometric reading rather than a boost pressure (candidate name barometric_pressure_selected; not proposed, since the selection between the live value and its default on a fault is only read from two assignments).

Array typing (a type change, so a note only): the forced-reading words are one per sensor slot, 2 bytes each, starting at 0x40bc80 (slot 4 = 0x40bc88 = battery_voltage_adc_forced_reading, slot 69 = 0x40bd0a = DAT_0040bd0a, the battery temperature slot read by cm848_sciCommand20Callback case 1); the matching override enables are bit (slot mod 16) of word (slot / 16) of diagnostic_service_dispatch_table starting at +72.
